- IllegalArgumentException: Thrown if the method is an instance method and obj is not an instance (but here obj is null, so that would cause NullPointerException instead per docs), or if argument number/type mismatches. Since the method was obtained with exact parameter types and the argument is of type KylinConfig, argument mismatch is unlikely. Also, if the method is static (as expected), null obj is ignored. Therefore, this exception is avoided under the assumption that the method is static and the argument matches.
- InvocationTargetException: Thrown if the underlying method itself throws an exception. The code has no control over the invoked method's behavior, so this exception cannot be avoided. It will be wrapped in InvocationTargetException.
- NullPointerException: Thrown if obj is null and the method is an instance method. The code passes null for obj, assuming the method is static. However, there is no check to confirm the method is static. If the method happens to be an instance method (e.g., due to class design error), NullPointerException will be thrown. This condition is not avoided.
- ExceptionInInitializerError: Thrown if the initialization provoked by this method fails. Since Class.forName initializes the class (single-argument version), the class is already initialized before the invoke call. Therefore, no further initialization is provoked, and this exception is avoided.

In summary, the exceptions that are not avoided are IllegalAccessException, InvocationTargetException, and NullPointerException.
